title: Choose Tavern's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Key Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Key Board
options.lineage: Inn reception key cabinets: numbered hooks, colored fob tags
options.thesis: Access is a key on a hook: issued, coded by color, numbered, returned on revoke.
options.viewport: A cool steel-gray workspace; every item carries a stamped reference number and a fob-shaped type tag; roles read as fob colors.
options.risk: Fob colors can turn into confetti unless each hue is locked to one meaning (role or item type).

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.lineage: Airport sign systems: yellow bands, black humanist sans, arrows
options.thesis: Onboarding as wayfinding: yellow is reserved for 'where to go next' and nothing else.
options.case: Strong product clarity for onboarding and navigation; yellow bands must be rationed or the dense hub becomes loud.

options.label: Dense Module Grid
options.lineage: Japanese high-density web: hairline modules, small red header tabs
options.thesis: Every project's sources of truth on one packed, ruled screen; nothing wastes a pixel.
options.case: Fits power users scanning many links; risks crowding new members who need a calm first path.

options.label: Tabbed Manual
options.lineage: Boxed-software manuals: colored divider tabs, acetate leaves
options.thesis: A project is a binder; categories are stepped colored tabs down the edge.
options.case: Tabs map well to categories; the acetate layering is heavy for a daily operational tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Modern B2B SaaS done straight: neutral grays, one blue accent, sidebar and tables at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, project header, filterable knowledge list.
